title: The @State Property Wrapper
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the @state property wrapper in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply local view state in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on the @state property wrapper and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Local view state”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Application code connects state, UI, APIs, data storage and platform capabilities. Clear ownership and explicit failure states make the experience more reliable and accessible.

content_blocks.title: SwiftUI State Flow
content_blocks.alt_text: The flow shows state ownership, a user action, a state mutation and SwiftUI recomputing the affected view description.
content_blocks.caption: State changes drive a new declarative view description.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** SwiftUI describes the interface as a hierarchy of views derived from state. Keep state ownership clear, compose reusable views, and verify keyboard, accessibility, and size-adaptation behavior.

**Work through the lesson.** Keep SwiftUI state ownership and data flow predictable while composing reusable screens and architecture. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.
